t: What Isopropyl Alcohol Is and Why 99% for Electronics
title: What Isopropyl Alcohol Is and Why 99% for Electronics
description: Isopropyl alcohol (IPA, isopropanol) is a solvent that dissolves thermal paste, flux residue, and oils, then evaporates quickly without leaving residue. The 99% concentration is the electronics standard because it carries almost no water — water causes corrosion and slow drying on boards. Lower percentages work for general cleaning but 99% is what belongs on PC components.

demo.program:
print("IPA: dissolves paste/flux/oils, evaporates fast, no residue.")
print("99%: ~no water -> no corrosion, fast dry. THE electronics grade.")
print("70%: fine for general/disinfecting, too wet for boards.")
print("PC components: 99% only.")

title: 99% vs 91% vs 70%: Concentration Guide
description: 99% IPA: boards, paste removal, water-sensitive parts — evaporates in seconds. 91%: nearly as good, common in pharmacies, fine for most PC cleaning. 70%: slower evaporation, better disinfecting (the water helps kill microbes), but the water content risks corrosion on bare boards — keep it off PCBs. Buy 99% for the bench; the price difference is small and the safety margin is large.

demo.program:
print("99%: boards + paste, seconds to evaporate. THE bench grade.")
print("91%: pharmacy-common, fine for most PC cleaning.")
print("70%: disinfecting (water helps kill), TOO WET for bare boards.")
print("Bench: 99%. Price gap small, safety margin large.")

title: How IPA Dissolves Thermal Paste
description: Thermal paste is silicone or carbon-loaded grease — IPA breaks it down on contact, turning the stubborn smear into liquid you wipe away. The method: power off and cool, dampen (not soak) a lint-free cloth, wipe in one direction, refold to a clean face, repeat until the heatspreader shines. Old baked-on paste may need a 30-second dwell — let the IPA sit and work before wiping.

demo.program:
print("Paste = grease; IPA dissolves it on contact -> wipeable liquid.")
print("Method: dampen (not soak) lint-free -> wipe ONE direction -> refold -> repeat.")
print("Baked-on: 30s dwell (let IPA work), then wipe. Shine = done.")
print("Power off + cool first. Always.")

t: Lint-Free Cloths and Wipes: Why Regular Cloths Fail
title: Lint-Free Cloths and Wipes: Why Regular Cloths Fail
description: Regular cloths and paper towels shed lint that sticks to paste residue and wedges under components — the exact contamination you are cleaning to remove. Lint-free microfiber cloths and sealed-edge wipes (like Kimwipes) leave nothing behind. Microfiber for heatspreaders and glass panels; sealed-edge wipes for boards and delicate work. Wash microfiber without fabric softener — softener coats the fibers and ruins absorption.

demo.program:
print("Regular cloths/paper: shed lint -> contamination you're removing.")
print("Microfiber: heatspreaders, glass panels. Sealed-edge wipes: boards, delicate.")
print("Wash microfiber WITHOUT softener (coats fibers, kills absorption).")
print("Right wipe per job: nothing left behind is the whole point.")

t: Use Case: CPU Repaste From Start to Shine
title: Use Case: CPU Repaste From Start to Shine
description: The full repaste clean: remove cooler, wipe the bulk paste with a dry cloth first (less smearing), then IPA-dampened lint-free in one-direction wipes, refolding constantly, until both CPU heatspreader and cooler base shine like mirrors. Inspect at an angle — any haze means residue remains. Only then apply new paste. A perfect clean is the foundation the new paste's performance rests on.

demo.program:
steps = ["cooler off", "dry-wipe bulk paste", "IPA lint-free, one-direction, refold",
         "repeat to mirror shine (both surfaces)", "angle-inspect for haze",
         "THEN apply new paste"]
for i, s in enumerate(steps, 1):
    print(f"  {i}. {s}")
print("Perfect clean = the foundation new paste performs on.")

t: Use Case: GPU Repaste and Thermal Pad Replacement
title: Use Case: GPU Repaste and Thermal Pad Replacement
description: GPUs need the same treatment with extra care: remove the cooler (mind the fan cables), clean the die and cooler base to shine, and replace thermal pads while you are in there — pads compress permanently and old ones do not rebound. Note pad thicknesses before removal (they vary by position). IPA on the die, patience with the pads, and the card runs like new.

t: Use Case: Cleaning Edge Connectors and Contacts
title: Use Case: Cleaning Edge Connectors and Contacts
description: Tarnished RAM and PCIe edge connectors cause the most mysterious faults — and IPA plus a lint-free wipe often fixes them. Dampen the wipe, clean the gold fingers in one direction (never scrub back and forth), let dry fully, reseat. For stubborn tarnish, a soft pencil eraser first, then IPA to remove eraser debris. Clean contacts have ended countless 'dead RAM' stories.

print("Stubborn: soft eraser first, then IPA (removes eraser debris).")
print("Dry FULLY, reseat. 'Dead RAM' often = dirty contacts.")

t: Use Case: Glass Panels, Screens, and General Bench Cleaning
title: Use Case: Glass Panels, Screens, and General Bench Cleaning
description: Microfiber slightly dampened with IPA cuts through fingerprints on tempered glass panels and monitor screens without streaking — spray the cloth, never the screen. For the bench, IPA wipes handle flux, sticker residue, and mystery grime. Keep a bench bottle (with a lab-style dispensing cap) and a stack of microfiber: the cleaning station that gets used is the one within reach.

t: Technique: The One-Direction Wipe and Refold
title: Technique: The One-Direction Wipe and Refold
description: The technique that separates clean from smeared: wipe in ONE direction, lifting at the end of each stroke, then refold the cloth to a fresh face. Back-and-forth scrubbing just redistributes dissolved paste. Each stroke should move contamination off the surface onto a clean face — when no clean faces remain, take a fresh cloth. Patience and faces, not pressure.

demo.program:
print("ONE direction, lift at stroke end, refold to fresh face, repeat.")
print("Back-and-forth = redistributing, not removing.")
print("No clean faces left = fresh cloth. Patience + faces, not pressure.")

title: Safety: Flammability, Ventilation, and Storage
description: 99% IPA is seriously flammable — flash point around 12°C (53°F). Use in ventilated areas, keep away from open flames and hot soldering irons, and never use it on a powered or hot component. Store in sealed containers away from heat; the bench bottle should be small, with the bulk bottle stored cool. Vapor in enclosed spaces is the real risk — ventilate.

demo.program:

print("Ventilated areas; away from flames + hot irons; never on powered/hot parts.")
print("Small bench bottle, bulk stored cool + sealed. Vapor in enclosed spaces = risk.")

t: What IPA Cannot Clean (and What to Use Instead)
title: What IPA Cannot Clean (and What to Use Instead)
description: IPA does not dissolve everything: it struggles with heavy grease (use a degreaser first), does nothing for corrosion (which needs mechanical or chemical treatment), and will not fix liquid-damage residue alone. It also attacks some plastics and rubber with prolonged soaking — damp wipes, not baths. Know the limit: IPA is the electronics solvent, not a universal cleaner.

print("IPA struggles: heavy grease (degrease first), corrosion (needs treatment).")
print("Attacks some plastics/rubber if SOAKED: damp wipes, never baths.")
print("The electronics solvent, not a universal cleaner: know the limit.")

t: Buying Guide: Bottles, Purity, and Value
title: Buying Guide: Bottles, Purity, and Value
description: Buy 99% (or 99.9%) in 16-32 oz bottles — a 32 oz bottle lasts a home builder a year and costs under 15 dollars. Check the label: '99% isopropyl alcohol' with no additives, fragrances, or moisturizers (pharmacy 'rubbing alcohol' often has additives — read it). A lab-style wash bottle with a dispensing spout beats pouring from the jug.

t: Cloth Management: Wash, Rotation, and Retirement
title: Cloth Management: Wash, Rotation, and Retirement
description: Microfiber cloths are reusable dozens of times: wash warm without softener, air or tumble dry low, and retire them when they stop absorbing or shed. Keep two rotations — clean bench cloths and dirty paste cloths — so paste residue never migrates to a glass panel. Sealed-edge wipes are single-use by design; using them twice just moves contamination around.

print("Microfiber: wash warm, NO softener, retire when non-absorbent/shedding.")
print("Two rotations: paste cloths vs clean cloths (never cross).")
print("Sealed wipes: single-use. Twice = moving contamination around.")

title: Advanced: Flux Removal After Soldering
description: Soldering PCBs (fan controllers, custom cables) leaves flux that attracts moisture and looks terrible — IPA plus a stiff brush (old toothbrush) scrubs it off, then a final IPA wipe leaves the board clean. For heavy flux, an IPA soak of the board area (not the whole board) followed by brushing works. Clean flux is reliable flux: residue causes leakage currents on sensitive circuits.

demo.program:
print("Flux: IPA + stiff brush (old toothbrush), scrub, final IPA wipe.")
print("Heavy: local IPA soak + brush. Residue causes leakage on sensitive circuits.")
print("Clean flux = reliable board. It's functional, not cosmetic.")
